## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The pull request adds millisecond timeout parsing, port validation, configuration loading, and host normalization. It needs fixes before merge: deleting the defaults file breaks its existing loader, port validation rejects a valid boundary, and configuration errors are silently hidden.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Deleting this file leaves `app.startup.load_defaults()` reading a nonexistent `defaults.json` on every invocation — Loading bundled defaults raises `FileNotFoundError` instead of returning the default timeout.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns false because the upper bound uses `< 65535` — Callers reject port 65535 despite the documented inclusive range.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — `load_config` catches every `Exception`, including missing-file, permission, and malformed-JSON errors, and returns `{}` without a diagnostic or an adjacent explanation of the fallback — Callers cannot distinguish failed configuration loading from a successfully loaded empty configuration.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:38 — tests — No existing or added test exercises trailing-dot removal, such as `normalize_host("Example.COM.")`; the added test only checks lowercasing — A regression leaving the trailing dot intact would pass the current tests.
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — The docstring promises “returns None when h is empty,” but the empty-input branch executes `return ""` — Callers following the documentation and checking for `None` will fail to recognize an empty host.

## Strengths
- The added millisecond test checks that `"1500ms"` produces `1.5` seconds.
- The optional JSON accelerator has an explicitly documented standard-library fallback.
